subject: Model improvement opt-out & prompt/response custody — DPA redline
messages:
From: Elena Park <procurement@acquine.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acquine.com
Date: 2027-07-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA draft and model-improvement opt-out

Hi Rafael / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this through. Attached is our standard DPA with the redlines we need for pilots in our regulated product line. High level asks: a clear no-model-learning commitment for customer interaction data, explicit assignment of prompt/response IP to the customer, and assurances around cross-border transfers (we need any processing/storage of customer content to be limited to US/EU unless otherwise agreed).

Two quick questions up front so we can triage:
- Do you have a separate process for providing ops evidence (KMS residency, subprocessor list, SOC2 pages) while we redline?
- Are there any Redwood-hosted telemetry channels that might still be used for model improvement unless explicitly opted-out?

I attached the DPA PDF. Can we get a high-level response by Friday so our legal team can queue next steps?

Regards,
Elena Park
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acquine Health
Attachment: Acquine_DPA_draft_v3.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <procurement@acquine.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-30T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA draft and model-improvement opt-out

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the draft. Short answers first:
- Yes, we can offer a contractual "no-model-learning" commitment for customer content on certain plans (pilot/enterprise). That means we will not use customer prompts/responses to update or retrain any models or incorporate them into training datasets.
- Prompt/response output IP can be scoped to the customer (we typically provide an output-licensing clause that assigns output rights to the tenant for generated content).
- We can restrict processing/storage regions via Dedicated or Private deployment options; for Hosted we offer EU/US region selection and onshore KMS for enterprise contracts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly will propose short redline language for the DPA (two options: strict no-learn + narrow telemetry carveout vs. no-learn with anonymized telemetry allowed for service health).
2) We will share our subprocessor list and SOC2 summary via a secure link (we redact minimal ops contact info).
3) I can run this with our legal team for the scope you requested and return a marked DPA by EOD Wednesday.

Attaching our high-level dataflow diagram so you can see where telemetry collects (small attachment).

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_dataflow_diagram.png

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <procurement@acquine.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-31T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA draft and model-improvement opt-out

Elena — adding proposed contract snippets inline that should be easy to slot into your draft: 

Option A (strong):
"Customer Data. Redwood will not use Customer Content (including prompts and generated responses) to train, fine-tune, or improve machine learning models. Redwood will store Customer Content only for the purposes of providing the Service and fulfilling this Agreement. Any telemetry collected for service health will be aggregated and cannot be tied to Customer Content without Customer's prior written consent."

Option B (operationally lighter):
"Customer Data. Redwood will not use Customer Content to train or otherwise improve models except in aggregated, de-identified form for service reliability. Customer may elect in writing to opt-out of any aggregated telemetry use."

David — can you confirm we can produce a short attestation for (i) KMS residency options, (ii) list of subprocessors and locations, and (iii) SOC2 status link that we can pass to Acquine?

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <procurement@acquine.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA draft and model-improvement opt-out

Kimberly / Rafael / Elena — quick operational attestation below.

On 2027-07-31, Kimberly Park wrote: 
> Option A (strong):
> "Customer Data. Redwood will not use Customer Content (...)"

We can support Option A for Acquine's pilot under Hosted (dedicated-region) or Dedicated offers:
- KMS: We offer customer-managed KMS configuration for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted enterprise contracts we can provide onshore (US-only) managed KMS instances for key-wrapping and attest to key residency.
- Subprocessors: Current list (high level): Cloud infra (US/EU regions), Monitoring & Alerting (US), IAM/SSO (US). We will provide a redacted subprocessor inventory via the secure link Kimberly referenced.
- SOC2: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant; I will share our SOC2 summary and the relevant control mappings for data residency and access.

Operational notes: telemetry used for model-quality experiments is explicitly toggled off for customers with no-learning commitments; default-hosted service may collect anonymized metrics for capacity and latency, but these are never linked back to Customer Content. For the pilot, we will toggle the improvement pipeline off and provide an attestation PDF.

Thanks,
David Kim
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <procurement@acquine.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acquine.com
Date: 2027-08-03T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA draft and model-improvement opt-out

Rafael / Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the two options. Acquine's legal and security teams reviewed and we'd like to proceed with Option A for the pilot: strict no-learning + explicit customer ownership of prompts/responses. 

Action items we need from Redwood to close our internal purchase:
- Marked DPA implementing Option A (we'll start redlines on our side once we see yours).
- Attestation PDF for KMS residency and confirmation that the improvement pipeline will be disabled for our tenant during the pilot.
- Redacted subprocessor inventory and the SOC2 summary link.

If you can get the marked DPA and attestation to us by COB next Tuesday, we can fast-track procurement and sign the pilot SOW.

Regards,
Elena Park
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acquine Health
